stem:
Shaan fills three cells in a row with numbers. A cell is a supercell when its number is greater than each immediate neighbour. He wants only the middle cell to be a supercell.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: The filling $9$, $4$, $2$ works, because only the left cell is a supercell.
The filling $2$, $4$, $9$ works, because only the right cell is a supercell.
The filling $4$, $9$, $2$ works, because only the middle cell is greater than each immediate neighbour.
Any filling where $9$ appears is enough, because $9$ is the largest number he wrote.

teacher.key_rationale: Only 4,9,2 makes the middle cell the unique supercell. 9,4,2 and 2,4,9 make an end cell the supercell instead. Treating any appearance of 9 as enough confuses the neighbour test with largest-value alone.
